public_rationale: Launch records support important parts of Marcus's assessment: hallucinations persisted, and independent testing found genuine task failures. OpenAI also reported substantial improvements. These findings do not settle his blanket statement about every problem in the earlier post. Some referenced predictions concern later developments and cannot be validated by launch evidence.
limitations: The earlier post combines broad categories, specific examples, and long-term forecasts.
METR tested software-oriented capabilities and disclosed an NDA and OpenAI publication review.
No documented solution was found, but that absence is not sufficient proof of the universal claim.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT-5 appears not to have solved any of the problems Marcus predicted a couple of weeks earlier would remain unsolved.
conditions: problems he predicted would not be solved

statement.excerpt: I stand by my predictions from a couple weeks ago; none of the problems I said would not be solved appear to have been solved..

from_speaker: predictions from a couple weeks ago
our_interpretation: Assess the capabilities of GPT-5 at its August 7, 2025 launch.

The referenced July 27 post identifies unreliable behavior and reasoning, hallucinations and guardrail failures, unreliable downstream integration, lack of general intelligence, and unresolved alignment.
Read 'solved' as dependable resolution of a problem category, not improvement on selected examples. Preserve the tentative wording 'appear'.
The earlier post's predictions about future architectures and historical judgments in 2043 cannot be settled by the launch.
criteria.support_condition: Launch evidence shows that each applicable problem category identified in the earlier post remained unresolved.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Reliable launch evidence establishes that GPT-5 had resolved at least one applicable problem category under the earlier post's stated scope.
